title: Compacted outcome-signal map — personal sprint log
content:
Purpose:
A compact, high-signal scratchpad for tracking 1) personal outcomes I own this quarter, 2) a tiny set of observable ‘signals’ that indicate progress, and 3) quick weekly retros and experiments. Designed to be skimmable (1 page) and actionable.

Context / why this exists:
- I get distracted by feature tasks (bug fixes, code reviews) and lose sight of the measurable outcomes that matter for my promotion conversation and for the team’s roadmap (routing/cost controls for Dedicated).
- Instead of a long OKR doc I want a minimal scoring loop: pick 3 outcomes, pick 3 signals per outcome (weighted), score weekly, run micro-experiments, note blockers.

Quarter goal (Q4 2024):
- Outcome A: Reduce 99th percentile token latency for the s1 routing path by 15% without raising unit cost.
- Outcome B: Increase cache hit rate for common prompt prefixes in Hosted API by +8 percentage points.
- Outcome C: Make a visible x-ray dashboard for model-fallback decisions so SREs can see coverage (MVP for Console).

Signal scoring rubric (0-3 per signal):
0 = no movement / regressed; 1 = small change or noisy; 2 = solid directional improvement; 3 = clear signal & likely causal.
I cap weekly total to keep it focused. Signals are weighted; multiply score by weight and sum.

Outcome A signals (weights):
- A1: p99 latency on s1 path (weight 3) — current baseline 420ms -> target 357ms
- A2: % of requests served with fast-KV kernel (weight 2) — baseline 12% -> target 30%
- A3: mean tokens/batch on s1 at peak (weight 1) — small wins here reduce overhead

Outcome B signals (weights):
- B1: prefix cache hit rate on Hosted API (weight 3) — baseline 21% -> 29%
- B2: median latency for cached requests (weight 1)
- B3: number of prompt templates in top-50 corpus with a persistent cache key (weight 1)

Outcome C signals (weights):
- C1: Fraction of decisions logged with fallback reason in Console (weight 3)
- C2: Time to show fallback trace in debug UI (weight 2)
- C3: SRE confidence survey score (weekly micro-survey) (weight 1)

Weekly logs (compact):
- 2024-10-15 — Week 1
  * A1: 420ms (0) — no change after kernel revert; still investigating bloom filters.
  * A2: 12% (0) — kernel rollout blocked by infra config; opened JIRA-INF-4321.
  * B1: 22% (1) — added 6 prompt templates to cache list (manual), small bump.
  * C1: 5% (0) — prototype logging only in local branch; need backend hook.
  * Experiment: feature-flagged KV-prefetch in canary — rejected due to mem spike. Notes: tune prefetch window.

- 2024-10-22 — Week 2
  * A1: 410ms (1) — minor improvement after GC tuning on s1.
  * A2: 14% (1) — ephemeral rise after rolling back bad eviction policy.
  * B1: 24% (1) — automated template extraction script added (PR #88), needs more templates.
  * C1: 8% (0) — local logs now shipped; backend mapping incomplete.
  * Retro: too many interrupt tickets. Action: protect 3 hours/week for outcome work.

- 2024-10-29 — Week 3
  * A1: 392ms (2) — kernel selection fix landed; p99 shifted.
  * A2: 18% (1) — more traffic served by fast-KV on small files.
  * B1: 26% (1) — started rolling template dedupe job; noisy but positive.
  * C1: 12% (1) — backend hook merged to staging; still missing UI display.
  * Experiment: lightweight KV quantization path tested in staging — latency stable, memory unclear. Follow-up: mem profiling on dedicated cluster.

- 2024-11-12 — Week 5 (skip week 4 due to offsite)
  * A1: 365ms (3) — near target after kernel + GC + queue-batching tweaks.
  * A2: 26% (2) — fast-KV reach improved; more coverage on medium-length sequences.
  * B1: 29% (2) — within 1 point of goal after adding extraction + caching rules.
  * C1: 22% (2) — Console now shows fallback traces for 20% of decisions in staging.
  * Notes: team shoutout — Rohan shipped the batcher change that unlocked p99 gains.

Quick weekly scoring (example):
- Week 5 weighted score = (A1:3*3) + (A2:2*2) + (A3:1*0) + (B1:2*3) + (B2:1*1) + (B3:1*1) + (C1:3*2) + (C2:2*1) + (C3:1*0) = compute in tracker.

Micro-experiments (list & status):
- KV-prefetch window tuning — blocked/memory spike (postmortem TBD).
- Template extraction heuristics — staged, safe to run continuously if we throttle CPU. (PR #88)
- Fast-KV kernel opt-in per model size — rolled out canary for small models only.

Blockers & escalations:
- Infra config preventing fast-KV rollout across a subset of Dedicated pools (owner: infra; JIRA-INF-4321).
- Memory telemetry for prefetched keys not surfaced (needs SRE + runtime work).
- Console UI time constraints — deprioritized vs other product UI work; propose 2-sprint focused slot to land C1-C2.

Short-term TODO (this week):
- [ ] Add 10 more prompt templates from support logs into extraction list (30m)
- [ ] Pair with Rohan to reproduce mem spike on prefetched KV (1h)
- [ ] Prepare 2-slide update for team sync: p99 trend + what unlocked gains (30m)
- [ ] File backlog ticket to add mem/alloc traces to prefetched-key path (JIRA-INF-XXXX)

Personal retrospective notes (two bullets):
- When I protect deep work time I move outcomes; interruptions = slower progress. Schedule guardrails are working but need better async updates to reduce context switches.
- Experiments that change memory profile need an observable guardrail (automated kill/rollback) — propose small infra runbook to avoid noisy rollbacks.

Open questions / hypothesis to test next sprint:
- Does a small increase in batch size (2→3 tokens average) meaningfully reduce p99 without raising 50th percentile or cost? Hypothesis: yes, when combined with KV early-terminate.
- Can we use a cheap ML classifier to decide prefetch eligibility to avoid mem spikes? Prototype idea: tiny histogram features + threshold.

How to use this doc:
- Weekly: update the three signal lines, add one short experiment note.
- Monthly: export summary to my quarterly OKR doc for reviews.
- When reassigning outcomes: leave this doc as handoff notes (short, signal-weight map included).

Random scratch (ideas to capture quickly):
- Could we expose a "preferred kernel" hint in the model manifest so runtime can pick aligned kernels earlier? Saves selection time at the expense of compatibility checks.
- Low-cost telemetry: sample 0.5% of requests with full kv-prefetch trace for mem profiling.

End of file — short, messy, useful.
